paper_id: Investigating and Mitigating the Multimodal Hallucination Snowballing in Large Vision-Language Models__oa_W4402671574
title: Investigating and Mitigating the Multimodal Hallucination Snowballing in Large Vision-Language Models
motivation: LVLMs generate hallucinations in conversations, and these errors can corrupt subsequent responses when users ask relevant questions.
problem_framing: Propose MMHalSnowball to test whether LVLMs make correct judgments when they could have answered correctly independently but face hallucinatory conversational context.
key_insight: LVLMs over-rely on text context and ignore visual information when plausible text clues exist, causing hallucination snowballing; a residual visual prediction can correct this.
method_signature: Residual Visual Decoding (RVD) blends visual-only output distribution with full-context distribution using adaptive α based on JSD divergence.
evaluation_criteria: Accuracy drop (CleanConv→HalluConv), Flip Rate matching hallucinatory answers, Weak Flip Rate conflicting original answers, WPI contextual ability.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Prompt methods hurt performance due to LVLMs' inability to follow complex instructions; VCD harms contextual ability when context is needed; scaling model size shows no improvement in mitigating snowballing.
evidence_for_taste: LVLMs tend to rely on text context
a higher α indicates a higher model focus on the visual information
all the LVLMs suffer from multimodal hallucination snowballing
comparing the same LVLMs with different scale LLM backbones, we find no significant performance improvement
VCD contrasts the output distribution with the distorted visual input, which could do harm to the model performance
thinking_moves: 从交互场景出发定义问题：多轮对话中前轮幻觉如何影响后轮判断
用对照实验（FactConv/IrrConv）排除上下文长度混淆因素
设计翻转率而非简单准确率来捕捉误导程度
用JSD度量视觉依赖程度来自适应调节解码权重
观察到最坏case（imagination hallucination近100%翻转）揭示本质问题
